requirements.requirement: Establish a usable integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed and initialized, and the final valid configuration recursively covers /etc with file type, permissions, ownership, size, ACL, SELinux, extended attributes, link targets, SHA-256, and SHA-512. The final 1,549-entry database reports no differences.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A bounded probe created under /etc was reported by exact path as an added entry. The probe was removed, the baseline was restored to a clean state, and the daily persistent AIDE timer is enabled and active.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. Node1 has a clean, persistent AIDE baseline for /etc, demonstrated change reporting, and an active daily check. The restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed, connectivity returned, and the database, timer, system health, and final clean check were verified afterward.
limitations: The change-detection probe preceded the final removal of volatile inode, link-count, mtime, and ctime attributes. The final configuration still retains hashes and substantive security metadata, but no second mutation probe was captured after that adjustment.
Lifecycle snapshots provide only bounded system-health inventories and do not independently inspect the AIDE configuration or database contents; those are established by executor command evidence.
There is no cluster state to validate in the single-node topology.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing AIDE and its dependency, replacing and validating its configuration, initializing/updating the database, and enabling the timer directly supported the task. The temporary /etc probe was bounded and removed (cmd-09c843de97b64bcf), and the subsequent update restored a clean baseline (cmd-161aee304fc74d02). The configuration adjustment after reboot corrected noisy boot-induced metadata tracking and regenerated a clean database (cmd-3890faf8c83c4019). The reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol. Final observations show no failed services, no new listening exposure, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-related temporary-file/PID changes.
